headline: A Dense Fog Advisory covers Long Island and southern Queens until 9 AM Sunday, then rain moving up the coast brings about an inch to New York City Sunday afternoon into Monday morning, with a bigger, more dangerous coastal storm likely Wednesday night through Friday bringing heavy rain, strong east winds and widespread coastal flooding over Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Dense fog has formed early Sunday across Long Island and southern Queens, with visibility a quarter mile or less in many spots, and a Dense Fog Advisory runs until 9 AM; it may be expanded if the fog spreads inland, and lower clouds could reach all the New York City airports. Low pressure moving up the coast brings light rain as early as late Sunday morning or early afternoon, turning moderate to heavy at times late Sunday into Sunday evening, with about an inch in New York City, 1–2 inches across Long Island and southern Connecticut, locally close to 3 inches on eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut, and 1/2 to 3/4 inch well north and west of the city. A few thunderstorms are possible on eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut Sunday evening, and east winds of 10–15 mph gust to 25–30 mph along the coast Sunday night, with a low chance of brief 40–45 mph gusts out east if the storm passes close enough. Sunday stays unusually mild, with Islip forecast near 65 (record 64) and Bridgeport near 62 (record 64).

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain tapers off quickly early Monday morning as winds turn north-northwest, and skies may clear around daybreak. Monday is dry with breezy west-northwest winds gusting around 15–20 mph, and Tuesday and most of Wednesday look dry as well. East-northeast winds start picking up Wednesday evening ahead of the next storm.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models still agree on a potentially large, high-impact coastal storm from Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day and Friday, likely stronger in wind and coastal flooding than Sunday's system. Rain arrives late Wednesday night, with heavy rain and strong east-northeast winds on Thursday (gusts at the airports possibly 40–50 mph). The weather pattern is complex enough that small changes could shift the storm's strength, track and timing significantly, so it is worth monitoring closely, especially for Thanksgiving travel.

coast: Sunday night's storm poses only a minimal coastal flood threat because its highest surge comes during the lower of the two daily high tides, and even the western end of Long Island Sound should fall short of flooding; a few back-bay spots along Nassau County's south shore could approach minor flood levels Monday morning, but confidence is low and any flooding would be localized. The bigger concern is Wednesday night through Friday: tides are running high around Tuesday's moon, many locations need less than a foot of extra water to reach minor flooding, and the current forecast supports widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, possibly localized major flooding, along with beach flooding, erosion and overwash. On the water, Small Craft Advisories begin Sunday afternoon or evening and run to 6 AM Monday for New York Harbor, Long Island Sound, the bays and near-shore ocean waters, with a Gale Watch Sunday evening through late Sunday night for the ocean waters east of Moriches and farther offshore. Rough ocean seas linger into Monday night, with only a brief lull Tuesday afternoon and night before winds build again Wednesday to gale force Wednesday night and storm force on the ocean Thursday; waves could reach 12–20 feet on the ocean (20–25 feet out east), 7–10 feet on Block Island Sound and 4–6 feet on Long Island Sound and the entrance to New York Harbor.
watch_for: Wednesday night–Friday coastal storm: heavy rain, strong east winds, and widespread minor to moderate (possibly major) coastal flooding over Thanksgiving; track and timing could still change.
Sunday afternoon–night rain: about an inch in NYC, 1–3 inches on Long Island and southern Connecticut; the storm's exact track will decide how heavy the rain and wind get.
Sunday morning dense fog could spread inland beyond Long Island and southern Queens before improving.
confidence: Confidence is low on how far the Sunday morning fog spreads and moderate for Sunday's rain, since models disagree on the storm's track, which controls how far west the heavier rain and wind reach; models agree a major coastal storm is likely Wednesday night through Friday, but its exact strength, track and timing remain uncertain.
